name: Microabrasion
summary: A dentist-applied acid-pumice polish that removes a sliver of stained enamel; used for fluorosis and white spots.
lead: Enamel microabrasion is a cosmetic dental procedure that removes a very thin outer layer of enamel, using a mildly acidic abrasive compound, to reduce surface discolouration such as white or brown spots. The first practical method, using weak hydrochloric acid and pumice, was developed by Theodore Croll and Richard Cavanaugh in 1986.

name: Resin infiltration (ICON)
summary: A resin that seeps into white spots to arrest early lesions and blend them in; trials are many, outcomes not summarised here.
lead: Resin infiltration is a micro-invasive dental treatment in which a low-viscosity resin is infiltrated into porous, demineralised enamel to arrest early lesions and, as a cosmetic effect, mask white spots; Icon is the best-known commercial product. An encyclopedia article on tooth decay describes resin infiltration as a micro-invasive intervention shown to slow progression of proximal decay.

name: Whitening LED tray with red light
summary: A mouth tray with LED and red light sold to boost at-home whitening gel; light benefit in general bleaching is mixed and red-specific data is absent.
lead: A whitening LED tray with red light is a consumer device that combines a mouth tray, usually loaded with a peroxide-based or other whitening gel, with built-in light-emitting diodes, some of which emit red light, marketed for at-home tooth whitening. The light component is sold as a way to speed up or enhance the action of the gel.
claims: Red or LED light makes whitening gel work faster or better

name: Blue-light teeth whitening device
summary: LED gadgets sold to whiten teeth with blue light; light helps only as an add-on to peroxide in some studies, and light-only data is lacking.
lead: A blue-light teeth whitening device is a consumer gadget, often a handheld or mouthpiece LED unit, marketed to whiten teeth with light, sometimes with a gel and sometimes on its own. The category is tied to light-accelerated (power) bleaching in dental offices, which uses halogen, LED or plasma lights together with high-concentration peroxide gel .
claims: Blue light can whiten teeth on its own or much faster

name: Electric toothbrush whitening heads
summary: Polishing-style replacement heads for powered brushes; they can address surface stain, with no head-specific trials found.
lead: Electric toothbrush whitening heads are replacement brush heads marketed for use with powered toothbrushes to remove surface stains and make teeth look whiter. They typically differ from standard heads in bristle layout or a polishing cup or pad.

name: Teeth whitening Hollywood smile Turkey trip
summary: Travelling to Turkey for a veneer-and-whitening smile makeover at lower prices; documented concerns centre on enamel removal and aftercare.
lead: A Hollywood smile Turkey trip is a form of dental tourism in which a person travels to Turkey for a cosmetic smile makeover, commonly involving porcelain veneers or crowns, often combined with whitening. Turkey is described as a notable destination for dental work such as veneers, crowns and implants in cities including Istanbul, Ankara and Antalya, with costs considerably lower than in Western Europe .

name: Metal braces
summary: Classic fixed brackets-and-wire orthodontics; well-established for tooth alignment, highly visible.
lead: Metal braces are the traditional form of fixed orthodontic appliance: stainless steel brackets bonded to the teeth and joined by an archwire, held with elastic ties or built-in clips (self-ligating) . They apply steady pressure so that bone remodels around moved teeth, and are the most common type of braces .

name: Ceramic braces
summary: Tooth-coloured fixed braces that trade some visibility for the same bracket-and-wire mechanics.
lead: Ceramic braces are fixed orthodontic appliances whose brackets are tooth-coloured rather than metal, designed to be less noticeable than traditional metal braces. They work like other fixed braces, using brackets and an archwire to apply pressure that moves teeth .

name: Direct-to-consumer aligners (SmileDirectClub)
summary: Mail-order clear aligners that promised cheaper straight teeth; the flagship company went bankrupt in 2023 amid professional complaints.
lead: Direct-to-consumer (DTC) aligners are clear plastic orthodontic aligners marketed straight to the public, usually through an online ordering process in which the patient takes dental impressions or scans at home or in a retail studio and a dentist or orthodontist reviews the case remotely. The best-known example was SmileDirectClub, a Nashville-based company founded in 2014 by Jordan Katzman and Alex Fenkell.

name: Self-ligating braces (Damon)
summary: Braces whose brackets clip the wire themselves, marketed as faster and gentler; trial reviews have compared them against conventional brackets.
lead: Self-ligating braces are fixed orthodontic brackets that hold the archwire with a built-in clip or slide rather than with elastic or wire ties. They are described as the second most common type of braces, and the Damon system is one commercial brand of them.

name: Retainers
summary: Plastic or wire appliances that keep teeth where braces put them; forums debate whether they hold back jaw growth, which nobody has tested.
lead: Orthodontic retainers are appliances worn after braces or aligners to hold teeth in their corrected positions. Teeth can drift back toward their former positions (relapse) because of recoil of gum fibers, soft-tissue pressure, the bite and continued jaw growth.
claims: Retainers worn through the teen years can stop the palate or maxilla from developing.
Wearing a retainer at night reverses the progress made by mewing during the day.
Retainers are needed to hold teeth stable before or between jaw procedures.

name: Fixed lingual retainer
summary: A wire glued behind the lower front teeth to stop relapse; it stays put, but is harder to clean.
lead: A fixed lingual retainer is a thin wire bonded to the tongue-side surfaces of the front teeth, most often the lower front teeth, to hold them in position after orthodontic treatment. It is typically bonded to the six front teeth or only the canines, and is used where relapse is considered more likely, such as after correction of severe rotations or gaps.

name: Accelerated orthodontics (AcceleDent / Propel)
summary: Vibration, light, bone-perforation and surgical add-ons that promise shorter braces time; evidence for non-surgical versions is weak, surgical ones more effective but invasive.
lead: Accelerated orthodontics refers to adjuncts used with braces or clear aligners that aim to speed tooth movement and shorten treatment. They are commonly grouped as non-surgical methods, such as cyclic vibration devices (AcceleDent is one brand), low-level light therapy and micro-osteoperforations such as the Propel system, and surgical methods such as corticotomy, piezocision and periodontally accelerated osteogenic orthodontics.

name: Surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion (SARPE)
summary: Jaw surgery plus an expander to widen the upper jaw in adults; established for narrow-jaw bite problems, its facial-aesthetic value is mostly forum lore.
lead: Surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion (SARPE), also called SARME, is a combined surgical and orthodontic procedure that widens the upper jaw in people whose midpalatal suture has fused after puberty. A surgeon makes bone cuts to release resistance, after which an expander appliance is gradually activated to widen the maxilla.
claims: SARPE widens the maxilla in adults, which also widens and improves the face.
Non-surgical methods such as mewing or MSE stop working after adolescence or about age 25.
The procedure is expensive and may be classed as cosmetic.

name: MARPE (mini-implant palate expander)
summary: A palate expander anchored to the palatal bone with mini-screws so it can widen the upper jaw in teens and young adults without cutting the bone; studies show skeletal widening, but cosmetic effects are barely studied.
lead: MARPE (micro-implant or miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion) is an orthodontic technique for widening the upper jaw in patients whose midpalatal suture is no longer easily opened by a conventional tooth-borne expander. The appliance is anchored to the palate with mini-implants and is used to treat maxillary transverse deficiency, a narrow upper jaw associated with crossbite, crowding and, in some patients, nasal airway restriction .
claims: MARPE widens the cheekbones and midface
MARPE gives more skeletal and less dental change than a conventional expander
Expansion can make an already wide face look worse
MARPE is worth it even for small expansions such as 4 to 6 mm

name: Palate expander
summary: An orthodontic appliance that widens the upper jaw, mainly in children and teens; well established for narrow palates and crossbites, with cosmetic effects on the face largely unstudied.
lead: A palate expander (also called a rapid palatal expander, RPE or RME) is an orthodontic appliance that widens the upper jaw. A screw mechanism, usually anchored to the upper molars, is activated gradually to separate the midpalatal suture and increase maxillary width .
claims: A palate expander widens the face and midface for a better look
An expander is still effective at 16 to 18
Breathing problems can be cited to get an expander approved

name: Orthotropics
summary: John Mew's theory that tongue posture and oral habits shape facial growth, the root of 'mewing'; mainstream orthodontics regards the evidence as inadequate.
lead: Orthotropics is a theory and treatment approach founded by British orthodontist John Mew (1928 to 2025), which holds that the resting posture and function of the tongue, lips and jaws influence facial growth and that malocclusion is largely environmental . Mew framed this as the 'tropic premise' in 1958 .
claims: Proper tongue posture reshapes the jaw and midface
Orthotropic treatment gives better facial outcomes than conventional braces
Mouth breathing and tongue position affect ear and airway function
Mewing can cause jaw problems

name: Facial growth guidance appliances (Biobloc / Twin Block)
summary: Removable or fixed orthodontic appliances meant to steer jaw growth in children; Biobloc belongs to the orthotropics camp, and evidence for its facial effects is limited.
lead: Facial growth guidance appliances are orthodontic devices used in growing patients with the aim of directing jaw and facial development. The term is associated with orthotropics, the approach founded by John Mew, whose treatment system, the Biobloc, uses a palate-expanding appliance followed by a postural appliance .

name: Bimax / double jaw surgery
summary: Forum shorthand for surgery that repositions both the upper and lower jaw at once; an established orthognathic procedure with documented functional benefits and real surgical risks.
lead: Bimaxillary or 'bimax' surgery is orthognathic surgery in which both jaws are repositioned together, commonly a Le Fort I osteotomy of the maxilla combined with a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO) of the mandible . Wikipedia lists it among the main orthognathic procedures alongside genioplasty .

name: Genioplasty
summary: Chin bone surgery that moves or reshapes the chin; established oral surgery, discussed in forums as an alternative to double-jaw surgery.
lead: Genioplasty is chin surgery that changes the size, shape or projection of the chin. The term is used for operations that move or reshape the chin bone, most commonly a sliding genioplasty in which the lower border of the mandible is cut and repositioned, and it is also used more loosely for chin augmentation with implants. Surgeons who perform it include oral and maxillofacial surgeons, plastic surgeons and otolaryngologists.
claims: Sliding genioplasty can be enough instead of full double-jaw surgery
More millimetres of advancement gives a better chin
The surgery carries sensory risk

name: Gummy smile Botox
summary: Botulinum toxin in the upper lip muscles to lower the lip line; temporary, with many small trials.
lead: Botulinum toxin treatment for a gummy smile involves injecting the toxin into the muscles that lift the upper lip so the lip rises less on smiling and less gum shows. A gummy smile, or excessive gingival display, is commonly described as more than about 2 mm of gum visible above the upper front teeth when smiling.

name: Crown lengthening / gingivectomy
summary: Dental surgery that trims gum (and sometimes bone) to expose more tooth, used for gummy smiles when the gum line is the cause.
lead: Crown lengthening exposes more tooth by removing gum tissue and sometimes supporting bone, and is done for functional or aesthetic reasons, including gummy smile. Gingivectomy is the removal of part of the gum tissue and is described as the oldest surgical approach in periodontal therapy.

name: Lip repositioning surgery
summary: Surgery that shortens the upper lip vestibule so the lip rises less, aimed at gummy smiles from a hypermobile lip.
lead: Lip repositioning surgery (LRS) is a procedure for excessive gingival display, or gummy smile, in which strips of mucosa are removed from the inside of the upper lip and the lip is reattached in a more coronal position, limiting how far it rises on smiling. It is used particularly when a hypermobile upper lip is a cause.

name: Gum contouring laser
summary: Laser removal of gum tissue to reshape the gum line; a laser variant of gingivectomy with little direct study.
lead: Laser gum contouring reshapes the gum line using a dental laser to remove soft tissue, a form of laser gingivectomy. Wikipedia lists Nd:YAG, CO2 and diode lasers among those used, and notes proposed benefits such as a bloodless field and minimal discomfort, based on limited evidence.

name: Enamel reshaping / contouring
summary: Shaving tiny amounts of enamel to even out edges and chips: quick and subtle, but permanent.
lead: Enamel reshaping, also called enamel contouring, enameloplasty or odontoplasty, is a cosmetic dental procedure in which a dentist removes a small amount of the outer surface of a tooth to change its shape, length or edge, or to smooth chips and minor irregularities . It is typically applied to front teeth.

name: Dental implants
summary: Titanium tooth roots with decades of survival data, but they replace teeth and aren't shown to reshape the jaw.
lead: A dental implant is a prosthetic fixture, most often made of titanium or zirconia, that is anchored in the jaw bone to support a crown, bridge or denture. Modern implants rely on osseointegration, a close bond between bone and the implant material . They are used mainly to replace missing teeth.
claims: An implant plus a bone graft can thicken a weaker jawbone.
Implants can improve a recessed chin.
Implants might interfere with later jaw surgery, or damage the jaw.

name: Crowns and bridges
summary: Caps and fixed bridges that rebuild damaged or missing teeth; well-established, but they cost you tooth structure.
lead: A dental crown is a cap that covers or encircles a tooth or implant to restore its shape, strength and appearance, while a dental bridge is a fixed prosthesis that replaces one or more missing teeth by attaching an artificial tooth (pontic) to neighbouring teeth or implants .

name: Smile makeover / digital smile design
summary: A planned bundle of cosmetic dental work designed around the whole smile, previewed digitally first; pricey and mostly irreversible.
lead: A smile makeover is a planned, often multi-step programme of cosmetic dental work aimed at changing the colour, shape, size, alignment and display of the teeth and gums as a whole. It may combine procedures such as whitening, bonding, veneers, crowns, gum contouring and orthodontics .

name: Smile training / smile mirror practice
summary: Rehearsing your smile in a mirror: free and harmless, but no trials test it for looks.
lead: Smile training, or smile mirror practice, refers to deliberately rehearsing a smile, typically in front of a mirror or camera, with the aim of making it look more natural or attractive. No formal protocol or published trial of the practice itself was located for this article.

name: Smile maxxing
summary: Forum shorthand for optimising your smile, from teeth to expression; a loose umbrella with no formal protocol.
lead: Smile maxxing is a looksmaxxing-community term for optimising how one's smile looks, whether through teeth (whitening, alignment, cosmetic dentistry), the gums and lips, or the way the smile is expressed. Sources reviewed for this article contain no formal definition of the term, and no published research uses it.
